newsitem.title: USA: Refining turns round for Exxon, others see hope.
newsitem.headline: Refining turns round for Exxon, others see hope.

text.p: Refining operations at Exxon Corp showed a substantial improvement in the first quarter of 1997 and while others are hopeful, they are still waiting for better margins to turn into improved earnings.

Exxon said on Monday that earnings at its U.S. refining and marketing operations turned round to a $57 million profit from a $16 million loss and its non-U.S. operations reported $297 million profit, up from $190 million a year ago.
"The surprise in Exxon's results was overseas refining and marketing," said Steve Pfeiffer, analyst at PaineWebber.
Exxon shares, which had been up over two percent at 55-1/8 in early trade, were down 1/8 at 52-3/8 by the close of trade in a generally weaker market.
"This stock moves much more with the Dow than with its energy peer group, if Exxon had not been an energy company, it would have been down three points," said Fadel Gheit, analyst at Fahenstock & Co.
Schroder Wertheim analyst Michael Mayer said he had raised his year earnings per share forecast to $2.90 from $2.73, primarily to reflect higher earnings from foreign downstream operations.
Amoco Corp saw earnings at its petroleum products division slide to $28 million in the first quarter of this year from a restated $62 million last year as its plant ran at lower capacity.

"The decline in first-quarter 1997 earnings resulted from higher refining maintenance costs and lower throughput, reflecting the planned turnaround at Amoco's largest refineries," the company said in a statement with earnings.
Analysts said that the turnrounds hurt first quarter earnings by $50-$60 million.
The company declined to comment on the level of activity at its refineries but said that most were complete.
"We are starting to see some positive signs in the refining sector," a spokesman for the company said.
Amoco shares were up 5/8 at 82 by the close.
"We are seeing a definite improvement, Amoco was hurt by the turnarounds, and was doubly hit because it happened at a time when margins were improving," Fahenstock said.
A key element for both Exxon and Amoco were improved chemicals earnings in the first quarter of this year compared with the fourth of 1996," Gheit said.
Exxon's chemical division reported that sales rose five percent and worlwide earnings rose to $310 million.
At Amoco, chemicals earnings were below the year ago level of $240 million, but at $147 million were better than the $105 million of the fourth quarter of 1996.
Coastal Corp, which bunches refining and marketing operations in with chemicals, said the division lost $50.8 in the quarter, compared with a $34.8 million profit a year ago.
The company said falling prices and a mild winter in the U.S. northeast plagued the division.
"However, improving margins in recent weeks and wider sweet-sour crude oil price differentials indicate that Coastal has the proper strategy in this segment," the company said.
Coastal shares rallied 5/8 to 46 after the earnings.

Amerada Hess Corp first quarter net income per share plunged to $0.05 from $0.71, mostly due to the impact of its accounting first in/first out accounting proceedures, which left the company with a $56 million loss on its refining operations as a result of its 40 million barrel of oil inventory, compared with a $44 million profit a year ago.
Even at $0.05 a share, earnings came in better than the $0.03 forecast by analysts and the stock rallied 3/8 to 49-1/8. ((-- David Chance New York Newsroom 212 859 1902))
